connection: Session 21 can filter, order, project, and total clock entries. No WorkSummary type exists yet, so this session explicitly creates the report result before using GroupBy and Join.
objectives: Create the WorkSummary result type before querying into it.
Use GroupBy to partition completed entries by employee.
Aggregate each group into total hours.
Use Join to correlate independent employee and summary sequences by ID.

visuals.title: GroupBy creates one bucket per employee
visuals.explanation: Every completed ClockEntry is routed to the group whose key equals its EmployeeId.

visuals.title: Each group becomes one WorkSummary
visuals.explanation: Select converts a group key and its summed durations into a report result.

visuals.title: Join matches two independent sequences
visuals.explanation: Employee IDs connect employee names to WorkSummary totals without embedding an Employee object in the report.

visuals.title: The report is materialized deliberately
visuals.explanation: ToList creates the finished report snapshot after filtering, grouping, projection, and ordering.

preQuiz.prompt: What becomes the key of each clock-entry group?
Why must WorkSummary be created in this session?
preQuiz.explanation: The lesson must not assume a missing result type.

preQuiz.prompt: What does an inner Join produce for an employee with no summary?
preQuiz.explanation: An inner join returns only matching keys.

concept.title: GroupBy partitions before aggregation
paragraphs: After removing open entries, GroupBy(entry => entry.EmployeeId) creates one sequence per employee.
Each group exposes its EmployeeId through Key and its entries through enumeration.

concept.title: Select turns each group into a report result
paragraphs: WorkSummary is introduced explicitly in this session. It stores the employee key and total hours produced by summing that group.
Ordering by EmployeeId makes the report deterministic before ToList creates the snapshot.
concept.code:
.Select(group => new WorkSummary(
    group.Key,
    group.Sum(entry => entry.GetDuration().TotalHours)))
.OrderBy(summary => summary.EmployeeId)
.ToList();

concept.title: Join correlates independent sequences
paragraphs: Employee objects and WorkSummary objects are separate sequences. Join matches Employee.Identity to WorkSummary.EmployeeId and projects a display label.
Use the employee ID and name property names that exist in your current Employee class.
concept.code:
employees.Join(
    summaries,
    employee => employee.Identity,
    summary => summary.EmployeeId,
    (employee, summary) => $"{employee.Name}: {summary.Hours:F1}")

lab.objective: Create a WorkSummary result type, group completed entries into per-employee totals, then join those totals to employee names.
lab.startingCondition: Employee, ClockEntry, and the Session 21 LINQ queries exist. WorkSummary and ClockEntryAnalytics do not exist yet.
steps: Declare a public sealed WorkSummary class.
Add get-only EmployeeId and Hours properties.
Create a constructor that initializes both properties.
Declare a public static ClockEntryAnalytics class.
Stub HoursByEmployee with an IEnumerable<ClockEntry> parameter.
Filter out entries whose Clockout is null before calling GetDuration.
Group the remaining entries by EmployeeId.
Project each group to a WorkSummary whose Hours is the sum of GetDuration().TotalHours.
Materialize the report with ToList because this method returns a finished report snapshot.
Stub EmployeeLabels with employee and summary sequences.
Join employees to summaries by their matching IDs.
Project each match to a readable name-and-hours string.
Append a Session 22 App section that prints the report.

steps.text: Run App and verify the solution.
steps.code:
dotnet run --project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.App/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.App.csproj --configuration Release
dotnet build PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release --no-build

reveals.title: Solution
reveals.text: Use the Employee ID/name and Clockout property names established in your source.

lab.expectedBehavior: Production can report completed hours per employee using existing models and repositories.
lab.validation: dotnet build PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release --no-build

expectedFiles.why: Create the report result the old lesson incorrectly assumed already existed.

commit: session-22: teach grouping joining and aggregation
review: The lab uses production because that is the most natural environment for this concept.
Every referenced application artifact was created in this session or an earlier session.
Earlier production code, tests, and ScratchPad experiments remain intact.

postQuiz.prompt: Why filter open entries before GroupBy and Sum?
postQuiz.explanation: The aggregation must only call GetDuration on completed entries.

postQuiz.prompt: What does Select receive after GroupBy?
postQuiz.explanation: Each grouping has a Key and the entries for that key.
The shared identity establishes the relationship.

reflections: Why is WorkSummary a report result instead of another repository?
What does GroupBy remove from a manual nested-loop solution?
Would an employee with no entries need an inner join or a left join?
whatBreaks: Without WorkSummary the projection has no declared result type. Grouping before removing open entries lets GetDuration encounter incomplete data. Using the wrong join key drops or mismatches employee labels.
summary: Session 22 now creates WorkSummary before using it, then builds a completed-entry report with GroupBy, Sum, ordering, and Join. Nothing is described as pre-existing unless an earlier session actually created it.
